response.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT DISTINCT o.orderspivot, u.acctscope FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp), c AS (SELECT acctscope, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM matched GROUP BY acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total, order_count / AVG(order_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_per_scope FROM c

assumptions.assumption: Each order is counted once even if it has several risk/margin records (COUNT DISTINCT orders), since the request asks for the number of orders.
The average count per scope is taken over scopes that have at least one matched order. Scopes with no matches do not appear in the result.
users.userstamp is unique, so the user join does not duplicate orders.

alternatives.interpretation: Count matched risk/margin records (rows) per scope instead of distinct orders. An order with several risk records counts several times.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total, order_count / AVG(order_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_per_scope FROM c
